subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw expose a first-class bootstrap selector and dynamic command-expansion contract for sessions, and if so should it be limited to built-in tiers, config selectors, or plugin hook APIs?
rationale: The remaining request changes public config/API behavior and command-execution authority, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term product and security boundary.

options.title: Narrow selector/tier API first
options.body: Add a small maintained bootstrap tier or selector contract and defer command expansion until a separate security model is approved.

options.title: Plugin hook only
options.body: Route dynamic per-session context through documented hooks and keep core bootstrap loading limited to safe built-in files.

options.title: Full command expansion
options.body: Pursue bootstrap !command expansion only with explicit sandboxing, provenance, opt-in behavior, and upgrade-safe docs/tests.

recommendation.title: Narrow selector/tier API first
recommendation.body: Add a small maintained bootstrap tier or selector contract and defer command expansion until a separate security model is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for bootstrap resolution and session filtering points to steipete, and this decision needs product/API boundary ownership.
